epics[1].title.en: One hour of work: four edits to the instructions, and the rule that will keep them true

epics[1].why.en: The root cause is not the content of the instructions but the fact that NOBODY IS OBLIGED to edit them. This is the one conclusion of the skills audit that survived calibration completely, and the red team called it the most valuable in the file. The content itself is fixed faster than it looked: there are TWO genuine contradictions with your orders, not five, and each is a single paragraph.

epics[1].owner_sees.en: The instructions stop diverging from your orders, and knowledge about orchestration starts landing where the next agent on the next machine will read it.

epics[1].done_when.en: The list of contradictions with the Standing rules in force is empty; the agent-launch section refers only to tools that exist; seven skills are under version control; editing the skill is on the shift-closing checklist.

epics[1].risks.en: Editing the authoritative copy is automatically forbidden to agents — so this epic BEGINS with your decision, not with an edit.

epics[3].title.en: One engine for everything that has to happen regularly

epics[3].why.en: The root cure for R1 — fourteen findings from five auditors. And the trigger is ALREADY DESIGNED: the original research calls for a “PostToolUse async hook debounced on writes to docs/lab/”, and a PostToolUse hook is already installed in three places — the element simply fell out during implementation. Restoring it is cheaper than building a launchd timer, and more accurate in frequency.

epics[3].owner_sees.en: A dashboard fresh by the clock rather than by a wave boundary. A decision whose deadline passed at 3 a.m. is applied at 03:0x with no live orchestrator.

epics[3].done_when.en: Across a full day, generated_at is never observed older than the interval; a synthetic overdue DECISION is applied without a single agent session.

epics[3].risks.en: The new daemon must report into the same armed-check; races with agents are avoided by writing only through the existing atomic paths.

And the answer changed underneath us: the platform now computes status itself, so our own loop should shrink to whatever the platform does not provide.

epics[7].title.en: Autonomy that learns, and does not decide more than it should

epics[7].why.en: The manifest does not work as a source of decisions: three decisions cited a clause that does not exist, and nobody noticed. And the way the “a permission prompt ends the night” problem got solved was by removing all permissions.

epics[7].owner_sees.en: The digest can say “decided under YOUR rule N”, and that is verifiable. There is no class of question where the system decides about money or destruction on its own.

epics[7].done_when.en: lab-emit decision rejects a non-existent rule; a synthetic “spend money” question drops into tier 2 regardless of any flag; the digest separates “under the manifest” from “by delegation”.
